pulls.title: LOCMAF v0.3: genBox + full/delta header redesign
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
## What

Reworks the draft around a self-delimiting element sequence — zero or more `genBox` elements (any box outside `moof`: `styp`, `prft`, `emsg`, `uuid`, carried verbatim), exactly one full or delta `moof` header, then the raw `mdat` payload — and bumps `locmafVersion` to `"0.3"`.

## Highlights

- **Integer notation**: MOQT vi64 (Section 1.4.1) throughout; signed values as zigzag vi64. Full 32-bit `sample_flags` carried (compact 5-bit form dropped).
- **Canonical CMAF reconstruction** defined as a function of *effective values* (not wire presence), plus a canonical encoding for encode-side golden vectors. `saio` offsets are moof-relative, version 0; reconstructed boxes never need 64-bit sizes. CENC `senc`/`saiz`/`saio` reconstruction cross-checked against ISO/IEC 23001-7:2023 and Bento4.
- **Simpler DRM**: scheme-agnostic (`cbc1`/`cens` carried with explicit IVs); the cenc IV counter-prediction rule is dropped — per-sample IVs are always explicit; `cbcs` (constant IV) remains the only scheme-specific case.
- **Simpler timeline handling**: delta headers never carry an absolute `tfdtBaseMediaDecodeTime`; a BMDT discontinuity re-anchors with a mid-group full header. Parity exceptions drop from four to three.
- **Transport rules**: one subgroup per group, no datagram forwarding, delta state resets on gaps.
- **Catalog**: `locmaf` packaging is signaled in CMSF catalogs only, mirroring `cmaf`, with a conditional `locmafVersion` track field.
- **New informative section**: minimal self-framing for use outside MOQT (vi64 length-prefixed Objects) covering on-disk storage, LL-DASH, and LL-HLS parts.
- Consumption described generically via chunk and frame interfaces; single author, with Hugo Björs credited in the acknowledgments.

pulls.title: Carry the mfhd sequence number with a delta-coded step
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
LOCMAF has so far reconstructed every chunk with `mfhd.sequence_number = 0`. This PR carries the source value instead.

## Why

C2PA live video (2.4, §19.4.1) can use the `mfhd` `sequence_number` as the segment `sequenceNumber`, and the signed segment hash covers the `moof` bytes unless the signer excludes them. A reconstruction that writes 0 can never match such a hash.

## Wire format

- `mfhdSequenceNumber` (ID 18): the absolute value. It appears only in full headers, is sent only when it is not 0, and must not exceed `0xFFFFFFFF`.
- `mfhdSequenceNumberStep` (ID 20): appears only in delta headers and is delta-coded like any scalar field. A full header resets it to 0.
- A delta chunk's number is the previous chunk's number plus the step, modulo 2^32.

Cost for the two common packager patterns:

- Same number in every chunk of a segment (livesim2 `--c2pa`, moqlivemock): nothing beyond the full header.
- +1 per chunk (ffmpeg counts moofs): one two-byte field in the first delta header of each group.

Jumps, decreases and resets are step changes, or a full header. CMAF §7.5.15 allows values that repeat or decrease.

## Versioning

The extensibility rule now separates decoding from canonical bytes. A new field can be added within a version when ignoring it still gives *decode-equivalent* output: the same samples, timing, sample flags and decryption parameters. Only an extension that changes what the samples decode to needs a new `locmafVersion`.

A receiver that skips IDs 18 and 20 writes `sequence_number = 0`. The chunk plays but is not canonical, so `locmafVersion` stays `"0.3"`.

## Other changes

- Header-kind restrictions in the parity section, now four fields.
- Field table, with `mfhd` rows first.
- Full-header emission rule for ID 18.
- Effective values and the canonical `mfhd` rule.
- One canonical-encoding rule: the step changes only through deltas, never through deletion.
- Range checks in Security Considerations.
- Informative reference to the C2PA 2.4 specification.

The implementations (`Eyevinn/locmaf`, moqlivemock, warp-player) still write 0 and will follow separately.

pulls.title: Cite MOQT -23, LOC -05 and the current ISO editions
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Updates the references to the latest published versions and fixes two wrong CMAF clause numbers.

## IETF drafts

- **MOQT -18 → -23.** The vi64 encoding is unchanged but moved from Section 1.4.1 to Section 8.1, so the citation now points there. -23 renames Forwarding Preference to Delivery Mode, so the ban on Datagram delivery now reads "MUST NOT use the Datagram Delivery Mode".
- **LOC -02 → -05.** Section 2.3 still defines the even/odd property scheme that LOCMAF reuses.
- **MSF and CMSF** stay at -01, still the latest published versions.

## ISO standards

- **ISO BMFF:** 14496-12:2024 → 14496-12:2026. The cited clauses 8.8.3.1 and 8.8.5 are unchanged.
- **CENC:** 23001-7:2024 → 23001-7:2023. There is no 2024 edition; the 4th edition from 2023 is current, and the cited clauses 7.1 and 10.4 match it.
- **CMAF:** 23000-19:2024 is still current. Two clause numbers pointed at the wrong definitions:
  - "CMAF fragment": §7.3.2.2 (the CMAF track) → §7.3.2.4.
  - "CMAF segment": §7.3.2.4 (the CMAF fragment) → §7.3.3.1.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

pulls.title: Signal the LOCMAF version as a packagingMetadata key
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Replaces the separate `locmafVersion` catalog field with a `version` key in the MSF `packagingMetadata` track field.

## Why

The MSF editor's copy adds a `packagingMetadata` track field (moq-wg/msf#211, merged 2026-11-02). It holds `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, and the specification for the track's packaging value defines the keys. That is the job `locmafVersion` did, so a `locmaf` track entry now carries:

```json
"packaging": "locmaf",
"packagingMetadata": "version=0.3"
```

LOCMAF then adds no catalog field of its own, and CMSF only has to register the `locmaf` packaging value.

## What carries over

- The `version` key is required on a `locmaf` track.
- A receiver must not subscribe to a track whose `version` it does not support, or whose `packagingMetadata` has no `version` key. It may pick an alternative packaging of the same source instead.
- MSF requires receivers to ignore keys that are not defined for the packaging value, so later LOCMAF versions can add keys.

The other mentions of `locmafVersion` (the extensibility rule, the catalog summary, and the note on DASH/HLS carriage) now say "LOCMAF packaging version".

## Before merging

`packagingMetadata` is not in the published MSF -01, only in the editor's copy. This should merge once MSF -02 is published, together with bumping the MSF reference to -02.

## Follow-ups

- moq-wg/cmsf#27 drops its `locmafVersion` field definition.
- Implementations switch from `locmafVersion` to `packagingMetadata`: the moqlivemock catalog gate, warp-player, the msf-catalog-validator CUE schema, and the version strings on locmaf.dev.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

pulls.title: Add Related Work on ROHC and the low-overhead HEIF format
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Adds a short informative Related Work subsection (1.1) at the end of the Introduction. It places LOCMAF next to two earlier designs.

## What it says

- **ROHC (RFC 3095, RFC 5795):** the IETF precedent for LOCMAF's delta headers. Compressor and decompressor each keep a context, which packets carrying complete headers initialize, and later headers are sent relative to it. Because link packets can be lost or damaged, ROHC checks decompressed headers with CRCs. It repairs the context through feedback in the bidirectional modes, or through periodic refreshes in U-mode. LOCMAF instead ties its reference to a MOQT group, sent in order on one subgroup stream. A full chunk at the start of the group, or a later one, sets the reference much like a ROHC refresh. After a gap, the receiver resumes at the next full chunk or group.
- **Low-overhead HEIF (ISO/IEC 23008-12:2025/Amd 2:2026):** the MPEG precedent for a compact form that the receiver expands into standard ISO BMFF boxes. A single `mini` box replaces `meta` + `mdat` for one still image, much as a LOCMAF receiver expands an Object into a CMAF chunk. It covers one standalone image only, so it has no delta coding.

Three informative references are added: `RFC3095`, `RFC5795` and `HEIF-AMD2`. There are no normative changes.

## Why

Both techniques LOCMAF uses, delta coding against a shared reference and a compact form with a defined expansion, have published precedents. Naming them helps reviewers place the design. It also shows that LOCMAF's delta coding within a group is the part neither precedent covers.

For context, measured with libheif 1.23.7 (`heif-enc --mini`): `mini` saves a constant ~234 bytes per file. For a 128×128 AVIF, container overhead drops from 270 to 35 bytes. That fits keeping CMAF Header compression out of scope, since LOCMAF sends the CMAF Header once per subscription, not once per Object.

## Review notes

- The ROHC paragraph has been checked against RFC 3095: IR state (§4.3.1.1), LSB/W-LSB encoding (§4.5.1–4.5.2), modes (§4.4), residual errors and CRCs (§4.6), U-mode periodic refreshes (§5.3.1.1.2), and the context and context repair definitions (§2).
- `make`, `make lint` and the 72-column check pass.
